title: Choir and Hollow Anew
premise: Edmund Vasquez, a mercenary bound to a silent god and keeper of the Hollow Ledger Guild's accounts, takes in a feral child named Sera who speaks the First Tongue — the language in which the old gods were once commanded. The guild's rivals, a crown inquisitor, and the last priests of Edmund's vanished god all converge on her, each willing to buy, steal, or bleed for what she carries: not words, but the god's silence itself, stolen and hidden inside her. Edmund must choose between the ledger-law that kept him alive and the family forming around the girl. In the end he burns the ledgers, gives his sworn oath back to the dying god to buy Sera's freedom, and the found family carries her north through the first snow — alive, hunted, and finally their own.
about_author: Dominic Sandoval is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging ship manifests before turning to fiction about debts that outlive their debtors. He writes in harborside cafés and claims every story begins with an entry that doesn't balance.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unpaid Vows
chapters.summary: Edmund audits the guild's winter stores and quietly mourns his silent god, whose shrine candle he still lights nightly. A routine collection goes wrong when a debtor offers a strange child as payment. POV: Edmund. Beat: weary competence masking grief; the door of ordinary life creaks open.

chapters.title: A Girl Who Speaks Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Edmund refuses the trade but the girl, Sera, follows him home through the slush. She speaks a language no scholar in the guild recognizes — until blind archivist Maren hears it and drops a teacup. POV: Edmund. Beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into protectiveness.

chapters.title: Ledger Law
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane demands Sera be entered into the books as an asset or turned out. Edmund exploits a loophole to register her as 'carried debt,' buying time. POV: Edmund. Beat: the cost of cleverness; first hint that the guild is watching him too.

chapters.title: What Maren Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren reveals the tongue is the First Speech, used to bind gods before the Sundering — and that it was supposed to be extinct. Sera, warming to them, sings a fragment and the shrine candle flares. POV: Maren. Beat: wonder shadowed by dread; the secret becomes shared.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Winter Coat
chapters.summary: Crown inquisitor Halvard Vess arrives asking politely about 'unregistered persons.' He leaves a coin stamped with the silent god's face — proof someone knows what Edmund once was. POV: Edmund. Beat: cold fear beneath courtesy; the hunt has begun.

chapters.title: Bargains in the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Edmund seeks out Tessaly, a smuggler who owes him three favors, to move Sera if needed. She agrees — for the name of whoever taught the child the Tongue. POV: Tessaly. Beat: transactional warmth; found family's outer ring forms.

chapters.title: Sera Dreams of Drowning Bells
chapters.summary: Sera's nightmares leak power: frost blooms indoors, and she wakes speaking in a voice not her own. Maren teaches her grounding rituals disguised as games. POV: Sera. Beat: terror of self; tentative trust in these strange keepers.

chapters.title: The Last Priest
chapters.summary: A ragged priest named Odo finds them, claiming Edmund's god did not die but was silenced — and that Sera holds the silencing word. He begs Edmund to take it from her. POV: Edmund. Beat: temptation; the past demanding payment.

chapters.title: Corvane Opens the Books
chapters.summary: Corvane, pressured by Vess, orders Sera surrendered. Edmund discovers Corvane has been selling guild secrets to the crown for years. He says nothing — yet. POV: Edmund. Beat: betrayal banked like coals; loyalty tested by survival math.

chapters.title: Three Favors Called
chapters.summary: Tessaly moves Sera through the flooded undercity while Vess's agents sweep the guildhouse. Edmund stays behind to falsify the ledgers, erasing Sera entirely. POV: Tessaly. Beat: adrenaline and tenderness; Sera clings to a stranger who becomes kin.

chapters.title: The Word Beneath Her Skin
chapters.summary: Hiding in a lighthouse, Sera confesses to Maren: she didn't learn the Tongue — she swallowed it, fleeing men who cut words out of children. POV: Sera. Beat: shame transmuted into resolve; the secret fully revealed to readers.

chapters.title: Odo's Sermon on Silence
chapters.summary: Odo argues the word must be spoken aloud at the god's drowned shrine to free it — even though speaking it may kill Sera. Edmund refuses; Maren wavers. POV: Odo. Beat: righteous certainty colliding with love; moral stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Vess Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Vess arrests Corvane for obstruction and seizes the guildhouse, reading the doctored ledgers aloud with a smile — he knows they're false. Edmund is taken. POV: Edmund. Beat: the trap snapping shut; guilt over those exposed by his choices.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Vess offers Edmund a bargain: Sera for the guild's amnesty. Edmund stalls, learning Vess serves not the crown but a cabal of god-binders who want the word weaponized. POV: Edmund. Beat: defiance kindled; enemy's true scale revealed.

chapters.title: The Family That Isn't on Paper
chapters.summary: Tessaly, Maren, and Sera plan a rescue using guild tradecraft — impossible things traded freely. Sera insists on coming; she can unmake Vess's wards. POV: Sera. Beat: agency claimed; the found family chooses its own law.

chapters.title: Breaking the Counting House
chapters.summary: A heist through the guildhouse's forgotten vaults. Tessaly bleeds, Maren talks them past her own former students, and Sera frees Edmund mid-torture, her voice cracking stone. POV: alternating, anchored in Tessaly. Beat: cost paid in blood; victory without triumph.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Freed Corvane, ruined, tries to sell Sera's location to the cabal. Edmund confronts him; Corvane dies by his own desperate magic, and Edmund closes the man's ledger with a hand that shakes. POV: Edmund. Beat: justice outside the law, and its bitter taste.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Snow seals the passes. The cabal marches on the drowned shrine where Odo has taken Sera, believing sacrifice is mercy. The family races the storm. POV: Sera. Beat: dread and determination; all threads converging.

chapters.title: At the Drowned Shrine
chapters.summary: Climax. Odo prepares the rite; the cabal arrives; Vess demands the word. Edmund returns his oath to the silent god, and the god answers — briefly — through him, shattering the cabal's binding-circles. POV: Edmund. Beat: sacrifice offered; faith repaid in one terrible moment.

chapters.title: The Word Spoken Anew
chapters.summary: Sera refuses both surrender and death: she speaks the silencing word transformed — not to command the god but to forgive it. The silence lifts; the god withdraws willingly, leaving its power scattered to mortals. Vess, unbound, is taken by the tide. POV: Sera. Beat: catharsis; the war never reignites because she rewrites its cause.

chapters.title: Ashes Entered in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the guild lies open, Corvane's treason public, the ledgers burned. Edmund, oathless for the first time, registers nothing — and keeps everyone anyway. Maren begins teaching Sera safe words. POV: Edmund. Beat: quiet reckoning; debts forgiven, not forgotten.

chapters.title: Northward, Before the Snow Deepens
chapters.summary: The family — Edmund, Sera, Maren, convalescing Tessaly — leaves for the northern coast where gods are only stories. Sera laughs in the First Tongue, and this time it sounds like hers alone. POV: Sera. Beat: hope earned; the long winter falling gently on people no longer hiding.
